summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications move into production, where teams need to track costs, latency, quality, and failures that traditional APM tools can't surface. The right observability stack combines production tracing, cost analytics, evaluation, and alerting to pinpoint why AI systems fail and control runaway API spending. Adoption is trending toward consolidation with existing platforms (Datadog, New Relic, W&B) alongside specialized LLM-native tools.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chains, agent steps, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics—especially deep within LangChain/LangGraph applications.
features: Cost and token tracking per run
tools.pricing: Seat-based plus usage; Cloud starts at ~$39/user/month (approx. £80/month in bundled tier), with a free developer tier available.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem wanting tight, low-effort auto-instrumentation and robust evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, per-user and per-department costs, token usage, latency, and caching performance via a lightweight proxy.
features: One-line base URL change for setup (under 5 minutes)
Excellent cost analytics with per-user cost tracking
Zero markup on LLM costs as a gateway
tools.pricing: Cheapest option at ~£20/month; generous free tier and free self-hosting; request-based pricing with zero LLM cost markup.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the simplest setup and fastest, cheapest cost visibility across any LLM provider without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: Both ML training workloads and LLM application traces, token usage, evaluations, and model performance in a unified platform.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are usage/seat-based (custom enterprise pricing).
tools.best_for: Teams running both traditional ML and LLM workloads who want unified monitoring across model training and production inference.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, and model performance—bringing ML observability habits into LLM monitoring.
features: Root-cause analysis for model performance issues
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AX enterprise platform uses usage-based/custom pricing with a free tier.
tools.best_for: ML-mature teams wanting embedding/drift analysis and OpenTelemetry-based tracing across any stack.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, costs, latency, prompt performance, and evaluations with an open-source trace store.
tools.pricing: Free Cloud tier for <50K units, then ~£20 for 500K; self-hosted costs ~£30/month in infrastructure with ~2hrs/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Self-hosted teams wanting an open-source, cost-predictable observability stack with evaluations and alerting built in.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and traces using an OpenTelemetry-based standard that works across any stack and vendor.
features: Exports traces to any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, New Relic, etc.)
Open-source SDK with broad library auto-instrumentation
tools.pricing: Open-source and free; costs depend on the backend you export telemetry to (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, New Relic).
tools.best_for: Multi-framework or multi-vendor setups wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability backends.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy like Helicone or Portkey to enable response caching for repeated or similar prompts, eliminating redundant API calls and reducing token spend.
Route requests to cheaper or smaller models for simple tasks and reserve premium models (e.g., frontier GPT/Claude tiers) only for complex reasoning—model tiering can cut costs dramatically.
Set per-user and per-department budget alerts and spend caps so runaway usage is caught early; consolidate cost tracking into one observability tool rather than guessing from provider bills.
Trim prompt and context length by removing unnecessary system instructions, truncating retrieved context, and limiting max output tokens, since you pay for both input and output tokens.
